source.snippet: Setup: Keycloak acts as an identity broker with Azure AD (Entra ID) configured as a SAML 2.0 identity provider. On a shared, Entra-joined device, User A signs in through the app, then User B tries to sign in — but Azure AD ignores ForceAuthn and silently reuses User A's session, logging User B in as User A. This is a security issue on shared devices in enterprise environments.

problem_statement: Enterprise teams using Keycloak as an identity broker in front of Azure AD/Entra ID cannot force re-authentication on shared devices because Entra ID ignores SAML ForceAuthn requests, creating a security and compliance gap for multi-user shared workstations.
target_segment: IT/DevOps engineers and security teams at mid-to-large companies running Keycloak + Entra ID SSO with shared physical or virtual workstations.
notes: B2B/enterprise context — companies pay for SSO infrastructure and compliance tooling. The problem is a known gap between Keycloak and Entra ID behaviour. A targeted configuration guide, managed Keycloak module, or SaaS wrapper that handles ForceAuthn workarounds could command a service/consulting fee. Single data point today; needs volume confirmation.
